narrator.instruct: Gripping, energetic storyteller telling a true, funny science discovery story with wonder, brisk, excited and punchy, never calm.

penzias.instruct: A young scientist in 1964 inside a giant antenna, announcing with mock-scientific seriousness what the pigeons left behind, crisp, clear and quick.

dicke.instruct: A Princeton professor in 1965 slowly hanging up the phone and telling his team, half laughing, half crushed, that someone beat them to it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The oldest light in the universe is all around you, and two men blamed it on pigeon poop.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: New Jersey, nineteen sixty-four. Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson had a giant horn antenna.
lines.say: New Jersey, nineteen sixty-four. Arno Penzeeas and Robert Wilson had a giant horn antenna.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They wanted to hear the Milky Way.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But their receiver picked up a faint, steady hiss.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Day or night, wherever they aimed, the hiss stayed the same.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They aimed it at New York City. Same hiss.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then they looked inside the horn. Two pigeons were nesting there.

lines.speaker: penzias
lines.text: And a layer of white dielectric substance!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That's science talk for pigeon poop.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They scrubbed the horn clean and sent the pigeons away.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two days later, the pigeons were back. Accounts differ on how they left.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the hiss? It never changed at all.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So what hisses from every direction at once?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You see, the universe began hot and bright, in the Big Bang.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: As space stretched, that glow cooled into faint microwaves, three degrees above absolute zero.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It fills the whole sky, so the horn heard it everywhere.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In Princeton, Robert Dicke's team was about to look for that glow.
lines.say: In Princeton, Robert Dickey's team was about to look for that glow.

lines.speaker: dicke
lines.text: We've been scooped.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In nineteen seventy-eight, Penzias and Wilson won the Nobel Prize in Physics.
lines.say: In nineteen seventy-eight, Penzeeas and Wilson won the Nobel Prize in Physics.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They went looking for pigeon poop, and found the dawn of time.
